land.text: Essequibo and Demerara, official British territory from 13 August 1814 and part of British Guiana from 21 July 1831

successors.note: Held by the British in fact from 1796 (permanently from 1803). The infobox dates the Anglo-Dutch Treaty to 20 November 1815.

capitals.name: Fort Kyk-Over-Al (Bartica)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Fort Kyk-Over-Al (1616-1739)'. The coordinates are the confluence of the Essequibo, Cuyuni and Mazaruni, not on the page.

capitals.name: Fort Zeelandia (Fort Island, Essequibo)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Fort Zeelandia (1739-1803)'; the British held the colony from 1803. Coordinates not on the page.

correction.text: Fort Kyk-Over-Al on the Essequibo, where 'Led by Joost van der Hooge, the Zeelanders founded Fort Kyk-Over-Al'; building began in 1616 (infobox)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates the first fort to 1616 and the West India Company colony to 1621; Cliopatria's first Guyana cells are in 1622 inside its New Netherland row.

correction.text: the 35 Cliopatria cells west of 57.9 W (the Essequibo and the Demerara mouth), from the New Netherland row's wrong 1622 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The administration of the West Indian Company as well as the governor of the entire colony settled here in 1621.' The page gives no area or extent.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1629 western part (43 cells), which adds the Pomeroon coast

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page: 'Pomeroon founded in 1581, which had been destroyed by Spaniards and local warriors around 1596'; the 1629 shape's eight extra cells are the researcher's reading as the Pomeroon (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: 35 cells: Cliopatria drops the Pomeroon cells in 1653; the pages date no abandonment before 1689

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; the 1653 drop has no page.

correction.text: 32 cells after 'In 1689 Pomeroon was destroyed by French pirates, and abandoned'; British, French and Dutch hands alternate 1781-1814 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'After 1745, the number of plantations along the Demerara and her side-rivers rapidly increased', and 'a settlement was founded at the Demerara mouth' about 1780 (Stabroek, 1784), which Cliopatria's constant 32 cells do not show. Cliopatria has no Guyana cell in 1781-1787 and 1797-1799.

ledger.note: 1616: Zeelanders begin Fort Kyk-Over-Al. Infobox: 'Commencement of building Fort Kyk-Over-Al: 1616'; 'It was a colony of the Dutch West India Company between 1616 and 1792'.

1621: the West India Company takes the colony ('Established as a Dutch West India Company colony: 1621'; 'The administration of the West Indian Company as well as the governor of the entire colony settled here in 1621').
1665: the English occupy Essequibo. 'Essequibo was occupied by the British in 1665 (along with all other Dutch colonies in the Guianas).'
1666: the Dutch retake it. They 'retook possession of Essequibo under command of the commander of Fort Nassau Bergen in 1666'.
1689: the Pomeroon is lost. 'In 1689 Pomeroon was destroyed by French pirates, and abandoned.' Cliopatria's shape loses its last Pomeroon cells in 1691.

1781 (24 February): British privateers take Essequibo and Demerara. 'A group of British privateers captured Essequibo and Demerara on 24 February 1781, but did not stay'; the Berbice page has British forces occupying Berbice on 27 February 1781 in the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.
1782: the British lose the colony to the French (infobox: capture of Demerara and Essequibo on 22 January 1782).
1782 (27 February): the French occupy it. 'From 27 February 1782 to February 1783 the French occupied the colony.'
1783 (February): the French leave. 'The peace of Paris, which occurred in 1783 restored these territories to the Dutch.' Cliopatria's shape returns only in 1788.
1796: 'In 1796 it was permanently occupied by the British.'
1802: the Treaty of Amiens (27 March 1802) returns it: 'the Netherlands received the Essequibo colony for a short time, from 1802 to 1803'.
1803: 'after that the British again occupied it during the Napoleonic Wars' (the governor table has Robert Nicholson from September 1803).

1812 (28 April): under British occupation 'Joined with Demerara to form Demerara-Essequibo' (infobox). [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: counterpart british-colonial-empire -> demerara: the page says 'It was merged with Demerara in 1812 by the British who took control'; British rule is the occupation of 1803-1814 already in the ledger. Demerara has no dossier yet (listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers).]
1814 (13 August): the occupation becomes cession. 'Essequibo became official British territory on 13 August 1814 as part of the Treaty of London'.

1814 (13 August): 'Essequibo became official British territory on 13 August 1814 as part of the Treaty of London' (infobox: Anglo-Dutch Treaty, 20 November 1815). On 21 July 1831 Demerara-Essequibo was united with Berbice 'to create British Guiana'.

wars.name: British, French and Dutch contest for Essequibo
wars.outcome: British privateers took the colony in February 1781, the French held it from 27 February 1782 to February 1783, the Dutch were restored by the 1783 Treaty of Paris, the British took it permanently in 1796, returned it for 1802-1803 and held it to the 1814 cession.
wars.note: The page names no single war; the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War (1780-1784) and the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic wars are the context. The infobox and the text disagree on the 1781 capture (24 February 1781 versus 22 January 1782).

certainty.note: Plantation coast and river posts; the pages give no frontier, area or survey. The eastern boundary with Berbice and the western with Spanish territory are not on the page.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. The Essequibo and Demerara cells (35, then 43 from 1629, 35 from 1653, 32 from 1691) sit inside Cliopatria's New Netherland row, 1622-1796, west of 57.9 W; Berbice (east of that line) is the berbice dossier. The Demerara colony (a district of Essequibo until 1812, per the page) has no dossier of its own. One page opened (Essequibo (colony)); the first URL guess 'Essequibo_(Dutch_colony)' did not exist.
